### Summary

Windows allowlist execution could use workspace shadows. In affected versions, PowerShell command analysis could approve an exact executable from `PATH` but later run a same-named executable from the workspace directory.

This advisory is scoped to Windows hosts using exec allowlist mode with a PowerShell inner command and a workspace-controlled executable sharing the approved basename. It does not rely on replacement of the approved executable itself.

### Impact

If lower-trust content could place an executable in the workspace and steer an approved PowerShell command, OpenClaw could execute the workspace file instead of the allowlisted path. The process would run with the Gateway or node-host user's privileges.

### Patched Versions

The first stable patched version is `2026.7.1`.

### Mitigations

upgrade to `openclaw@2026.7.1` or later. Before upgrading, avoid bare executable names inside approved PowerShell commands and keep executable files out of agent-writable workspaces.
summary: Windows allowlist execution could use workspace shadows
